threats.title: How to we keep the password?
threats.description: Do we keep the password in the UI? Will it be output in plain text in a crash dump? Do we zeroize the password after user? Do we use a password safe string storage such as System.Security.SecureString.

threats.title: How validation work?
threats.description:
The WPF PDF viewer displays information about the signature of a document.
How does the signature validation work? What are root trusted certificates? Do we make a REST call somewhere to get root certs or do we use somehow OS to get root certificates? Does DPL has API to provide root trusted certificates?
threats.mitigation: Provide remediation for this threat or a reason if status is N/A

threats.title: Copy-Paste untrusted content from internet gets into deserialiser
threats.description:
When content is copied from internet, it will get into the deserialiser. Deserialisation could potentially instantiate malicious .NET types that elevate privilege.

The issue here, is it is really easy to copy content from internet, passing through very unsecure trust boundary.
threats.mitigation: We had double-checked the deserialisation about type safety.

threats.title: Connection String is of type string
threats.description: The connection string of the RadPivotGrid for the AdomdConnectionSettings is of type string. It also holds user + pass pair used to authenticate in-front of the Adomd server. This string could easily escape in crash reports and memory snapshots.
threats.mitigation: Evaluate if we could use secure string instead.

threats.title: XmlaNetworkCredential use SecureString for password
threats.description:
Currently the RadPivotGrid XmlaNetworkCredential uses the NetworkCredential base class from dotnet, that has overloads for its constructor accepting (string user, string pass) as well as (string user, SecureString pass)

Our class calls only the (string, string) base constructor.
threats.mitigation: Provide and recomend (string, SecureString) constructor overloads and avoid storing the password in a "string" at all cost.

threats.title: MDXQueryBuilder - verify string values are escaped
threats.description:
The MDXQueryBuilder uses the infrastructure for MDX expression for OLAP.
Since the engine to convert an AST to string query is in our code - dobule check for the "MDX version of SQL Injection". MDX is view-only, it does not support things like "drop table" as far as I am aware (double check that).
threats.mitigation:
There are some unit tests there - try to feed 3 ASTs like:
 - Select Name from Cube
 - Select Name, Surname from Cube
 - Select "Name, Surname" form Cube
And try to hack #3's single column value to generate a query that is supposed to look like #1 with escaped string, but when unescaped looks like #2.
